definition: Assigning a class label to every pixel of an image, producing a dense region map.
details: Assigning a class label to every pixel of an image, producing a dense region map. Architectures such as FCN, U-Net, DeepLab, and MaskFormer power scene understanding and medical imaging.

explainer.lead: Semantic segmentation assigns a class label to every pixel of an image, producing a dense region map. It matters because scene understanding and medical imaging need per-pixel classification, not just boxes.

tiers.eli5: It's like coloring in every pixel of a picture by what it shows: road, car, tree, person.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train architectures such as FCN, U-Net, DeepLab and MaskFormer on pixel-labeled data; a pitfall is that dense labels are expensive and errors at object boundaries are common.
tiers.paperLevel: The task of labeling each pixel with a class to produce a dense region map, commonly addressed by FCN, U-Net, DeepLab and MaskFormer. Limits include costly pixel-level annotation and boundary ambiguity between adjacent classes.

explainer.example: In a street scene, every pixel is labeled road, car, pedestrian or building, yielding a full segmentation map.
